es.summary: El AAS es un antiinflamatorio no esteroideo que inhibe de forma irreversible la agregación plaquetaria y alivia el dolor leve.
key_points: Inhibe irreversible la COX‑1 → disminuye la síntesis de tromboxano A2
Usado en infarto agudo de miocardio y angina inestable
Aumenta el riesgo de sangrado, especialmente con anticoagulantes
Interacciones con alcohol, tabaco y otros AINEs aumentan toxicidad gástrica

mechanism: Bloquea irreversiblemente la enzima COX‑1 en plaquetas
Reduce la producción de tromboxano A2, inhibiendo la agregación plaquetaria
Disminuye prostaglandinas, aliviando dolor e inflamación
indications: Prevención secundaria de infarto agudo de miocardio
contraindications: Úlcera péptica activa o historial de sangrado gastrointestinal
interactions: Potencia el efecto de anticoagulantes (warfarina, heparina) → mayor sangrado
Aumenta toxicidad gástrica con otros AINEs o corticoides
Alcohol y tabaco incrementan riesgo de úlcera
Puede reducir la eficacia de algunos antihipertensivos (IECA, diuréticos)
nursing_care: Evaluar historial de úlcera, sangrado y uso de anticoagulantes antes de administrar
Monitorizar signos de sangrado: hemoptisis, melena, sangrado gingival
Controlar hemoglobina y hematocrito cada 24‑48 h si está en terapia combinada
Retener dosis si presenta sangrado activo y notificar al médico
Registrar tiempo de sangrado de pinchazos o procedimientos invasivos
patient_teaching: Tomar con alimentos o antiácido para proteger el estómago
Evitar alcohol y tabaco mientras esté en tratamiento
Informar al médico antes de iniciar cualquier otro AINE o anticoagulante
Reportar cualquier sangrado inusual, hematomas o sangre en heces/orina
No interrumpir el tratamiento sin indicación médica

outcomes: Disminuir el riesgo de sangrado: sin evidencia de hemorragia en 48 h
Mantener hemoglobina ≥12 g/dL durante la hospitalización

interventions.action: Monitorear signos de sangrado (hemoptisis, melena, sangrado de encías) cada 4 h
Obtener hemograma completo y coagulación al iniciar y cada 24 h
interventions.rationale: Identifica disminución de plaquetas o anemia

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre evitar alcohol, tabaco y AINEs sin prescripción
interventions.rationale: Reduce factores que potencian el sangrado

interventions.action: Coordinar con el médico la prescripción de protector gástrico (p. ej., omeprazol) si hay riesgo alto
Verificar tiempo de sangrado de cualquier procedimiento invasivo antes de administrar AAS
Notificar al médico inmediatamente si se observa sangrado activo
interventions.rationale: Permite ajuste de terapia o suspensión del AAS

en.summary: ASA is a nonsteroidal anti‑inflammatory that irreversibly inhibits platelet aggregation and relieves mild pain.
key_points: Irreversibly inhibits COX‑1 → decreases thromboxane A2 synthesis
Used in acute myocardial infarction and unstable angina
Increases bleeding risk, especially with anticoagulants
Interactions with alcohol, tobacco and other NSAIDs increase gastric toxicity

mechanism: Reduces thromboxane A2 production, inhibiting platelet aggregation
Decreases prostaglandins, relieving pain and inflammation
indications: Secondary prevention of acute myocardial infarction
contraindications: Active peptic ulcer or history of gastrointestinal bleeding
interactions: Increases gastric toxicity with other NSAIDs or corticosteroids
Alcohol and tobacco raise ulcer risk
May reduce efficacy of some antihypertensives (ACE inhibitors, diuretics)
nursing_care: Assess ulcer, bleeding history and anticoagulant use before administration
Monitor for bleeding signs: hemoptysis, melena, gingival bleeding
Check hemoglobin and hematocrit every 24‑48 h if on combination therapy
Hold dose if active bleeding and notify physician
Record bleeding time after pinpricks or invasive procedures
patient_teaching: Take with food or antacid to protect the stomach
Avoid alcohol and tobacco while on therapy
Inform doctor before starting any other NSAID or anticoagulant
Report any unusual bleeding, bruising, or blood in stool/urine
Do not discontinue therapy without medical advice

outcomes: Reduce bleeding risk: no evidence of hemorrhage within 48 h

interventions.action: Monitor bleeding signs (hemoptysis, melena, gingival bleeding) every 4 h
Obtain CBC and coagulation studies at initiation and every 24 h
Educate patient to avoid alcohol, tobacco and unsupervised NSAIDs
Coordinate with physician for gastric protector prescription (e.g., omeprazole) if high risk
Verify bleeding time for any invasive procedure before ASA administration
Notify physician immediately if active bleeding is observed
interventions.rationale: Allows therapy adjustment or ASA discontinuation

summary.0.quote: Contraindications to aspirin are allergy to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), asthma, hemophilia, and other blood clotting disorders.

key_points.1.quote: Four classifications of drugs may be used in emergency situations for AMI and unstable angina: aspirin, oxygen, nitroglycerin, and, occasionally, morphine.

key_points.2.quote: The risk of serious bleeding in the stomach, gastrointestinal tract, brain, and spinal cord is increased with aspirin and other NSAIDs .

sections.mechanism.0.quote: Aspirin irreversibly binds to receptors on platelets, which prevents them from sticking to other platelets.
